free_tier.stated: Per-file upload cap 10737418240 bytes; files with zero egress are deleted after 7 days.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: The terms state a 10.00 GB maximum file size.

retention.stated: Files with zero egress are deleted after 7 days.
retention.notes: The terms state inactive file deletion is disabled and maximum file age has no limit; files with zero egress are deleted after 7 days.

egress.terms: Unmetered. Files served by GET /<sha256>, Content-addressed. Served through the server's own CDN; no egress counter is exposed anywhere.

interface_detail: Blossom (BUD-01/02/04/06) + NIP-96. Plain HTTP PUT /upload, GET /<sha256>, HEAD /upload for preflight. Pinned by NIP-94 kind 1063 events.
tooling: any HTTP client. Auth is a signed nostr event (kind 24242), so a locally generated keypair is the only credential. route96 (v0l), lotus, or hzrd149/blossom clients all speak it.
chaining: Content-addressed by SHA-256, so a chunk-per-object scheme maps onto it natively with no index server. The hash IS the locator.
limits_note: per-object cap stated in the terms. Retention is download-triggered: a file with zero egress is deleted after 7 days; inactive-file deletion is disabled and maximum file age has no limit.
reliability_note: single volunteer operator, no SLA, no durability warranty ('Do not use this service as your only backup'). Purges never-downloaded objects after 24 h, so a write-only cold archive decays to zero.

extras.quota_verbatim: 10.00 GB per file (hard cap, read off the server's own TOS page). No published per-user total. 'Inactive file deletion: No limit'. 'Delete never-downloaded files: After 1 days'.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap 10 GB. Retention is download-triggered, not time-based: a file nobody fetches within 24 h is deleted. Anything in the hot working set survives indefinitely.
extras.egress_verbatim: unmetered — files served by GET /<sha256>, Content-addressed. Served through the server's own CDN; no egress counter is exposed anywhere.
extras.chaining_verbatim: content-addressed by SHA-256, so a chunk-per-object scheme (BRIEF 2.1) maps onto it natively with no index server — the hash IS the locator.
extras.tooling_verbatim: any HTTP client. Auth is a signed nostr event (kind 24242), so a locally generated keypair is the only credential. route96 (v0l), lotus, or hzrd149/blossom clients all speak it.
extras.interface_verbatim: Blossom (BUD-01/02/04/06) + NIP-96. Plain HTTP PUT /upload, GET /<sha256>, HEAD /upload for preflight. Pinned by NIP-94 kind 1063 events.
extras.agent_focus: Relay/P2P transport networks that could carry bulk data without a central provider. For each: is data ROUTED (a real path) or is it only SIGNALLING (relay coordinates, bytes go peer-to-peer)? Free bandwidth? Can it carry 1 TiB/day (= 12.7 MB/s = ~102 Mbit/s sustained)? Identity gate recorded as the primary ranking axis.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
